title: Protobuf: Support to display JSON mapping for Protobuf message
description:
Add option display_json_mapping, that make a new JSON view of
this protobuf message displayed.

close #17797

If the you turn on the display_json_mapping (named "Display JSON Mapping for Protobuf message") preference, the items panel will display like: (note the items under "Protocol Buffers (as JSON Mapping View)")

```
Frame 16: 124 bytes on wire (992 bits), 124 bytes captured (992 bits) on interface \Device\NPF_Loopback, id 0
Null/Loopback
Internet Protocol Version 4, Src: 127.0.0.1, Dst: 127.0.0.1
Transmission Control Protocol, Src Port: 50051, Dst Port: 51035, Seq: 117, Ack: 226, Len: 80
HyperText Transfer Protocol 2
GRPC Message: /tutorial.PersonSearchService/Search, Response
Protocol Buffers: /tutorial.PersonSearchService/Search,response (Message: tutorial.Person)
    name: Jason
    id: 1001
    email: Jason@example.com
    phone: (12 bytes) (Message: tutorial.Person.PhoneNumber)
    phone: (13 bytes) (Message: tutorial.Person.PhoneNumber)
        number: 13588886666
        [type: MOBILE (0)]
    last_updated: Oct 13, 2020 23:11:26.000000000 ... (Message: google.protobuf.Timestamp)
Protocol Buffers (as JSON Mapping View)
    {
      "name": "Jason",
      "id": 1001,
      "email": "Jason@example.com",
      "phone": [
        {
          "number": "87561234",
          "type": "HOME"
        },
        {
          "number": "13588886666",
          "type": "MOBILE"
        }
      ],
      "last_updated": "2020-10-13T23:11:26+0800"
    }
```

You can copy the JSON by right click on the "Protocol Buffers (as JSON Mapping View)" item and select the "Copy->All Visible Selected Tree Items". If one line is too long to be truncated, you can get the full data of this line by copying the "Value" of this item in right click menu.

**It is useful to copy that representation to clipboard, which can be used to re-sending of message from command line in other protobuf tools.**

@crondaemon Hi, I have updated the commits according to your comments. Please help to check again, thanks!
Shouldn't the dumper be const (here and elsewhere)?
This can't be const, because we will invoke functions like `json_dumper_value_double` in those functions will change dumper->state member of `json_dumper`.

You defined this function in this dissector, with programmable scope, but you used it just in this single point. Maybe the scope can be omitted, and instead you can use `pinfo->pool`. If you are not keen to use this approach, I'd leave the scope programmable, but I'd use pool here instead of NULL, and remove the wmem_free.
OK, I will leave the scope programmable and use pinfo->pool and remove wmem_free.
